statements.text: In the second quarter of fiscal 2025, the company initially estimated a 3% of sales headwind from enacted tariffs. However, following the 90-day pause for non-China countries announced in April 2025, the actual impact was reduced to 1.5% of sales.
The company's primary defense is its highly localized manufacturing strategy, with 76% of its production occurring within the same region as its customers and 90% of its supply chain sourced locally.
To recover these costs, the company implemented pricing actions representing approximately 2% of sales in its Industrial segment, successfully neutralizing the impact on net earnings.
We anticipate that about one-third of this impact will be mitigated by sourcing changes by TE and our customers.
TE Connectivity (TEL) has demonstrated significant resilience to the U.S. "reciprocal" and "Liberation Day" tariffs introduced in April 2025.
